answer: In a timber auction network, the whisper registry activates an agent key only after a finalized transaction burns 10 tokens and names that key. A mirror of the registry checks the same burn records; each record authorizes only one key, so replay cannot create extra identities. Every additional identity destroys another 10 tokens, imposing a verifiable capital cost. Wealthy attackers can still buy many identities, and token price declines weaken the barrier.
